name: Joanna Wargala
bio: Joanna Wargala is a Polish Pro-Am dancer and entrepreneur, a former cellist who spent 20 years in business, from her first company at 18 to precious metals, before building the online dance platform Air Dance, now O-Dance.
about: In this episode, Marius Iepure sits down with Joanna Wargala, Pro-Am dancer and founder of the online dance platform Air Dance, now O-Dance, for a conversation about passion, vision and why it is never too late to start dancing. She won a cello competition at 16, studied in the UK and played first cello in a London orchestra, then spent 20 years in business before walking into a dance studio for the first time in 2016 and competing in London three months later.

They talk about why she built Air Dance to connect talented dancers from small towns with top teachers, the hidden costs of travelling for private lessons, why the dance world still runs on cash, the Dancecoin cryptocurrency and the Audance token pegged one to one to the dollar, dancing the Pro-Am final at the Royal Albert Hall, the Air Dance Christmas Ball during Dancing Week in Poland, her years in precious metals, side businesses for dancers, why online lessons should be a continuation of your lessons and never a substitute, why dancers, not teachers, judges or organisers, are the most important people in DanceSport, and the 3 a.m. wake-ups in Miami and the hypnosis session that told her to take dance classes.
teaser: Joanna Wargala on starting to dance as an adult, building an online platform for dancers and why dancers come first in DanceSport.
